"""
LRU Cache with Time-To-Live (TTL) Expiry

This module provides a thread-safe, LRU (Least Recently Used) cache that
automatically expires entries after a configurable time-to-live period.

Features
--------
* LRU eviction policy (most recent access is kept; least recently used is evicted).
* Per-key TTL (time-to-live) support: each item can have its own expiry time.
* Global maximum size limit (`max_items`).
* Thread-safe operations via a reentrant lock.
* Pytest suite included for the cache implementation.

Design Overview
---------------
The cache is implemented as a class ``TTLCache`` that internally maintains:

1. An internal dictionary ``_store`` mapping ``key`` -> ``CacheEntry``.
2. A ``CacheEntry`` object holding the ``value`` and the ``ttl`` (seconds).
3. A lock ``_lock`` to serialize access from multiple threads.

Key Behaviours
--------------
* ``put(key, value, ttl=...)`` – stores the value with a TTL. If the cache
  exceeds ``max_items``, the least recently used item is evicted automatically.
* ``get(key)`` – returns the value if present and not expired; otherwise
  raises ``CacheMissingError``.
* ``ttl_for(key)`` – returns the remaining seconds until expiry.
* ``expire`` – forces immediate removal of an item.
* ``clear`` – removes all items.
* ``size`` – number of currently live entries.

The LRU ordering is maintained by a doubly linked list of nodes. Each node
represents a cache entry and contains ``key``, ``value``, ``ttl`` and
``last_access`` timestamps. The list is ordered so that the most recently
accessed node is at the head (most recent) and the least recently used is at
the tail (least recent). When the cache is full, the node at the tail is
removed.

The code is written to be fully functional, documented, and testable with

"""
LRU Cache with Time-To-Live Expiry
================================

This module implements a high-performance, thread-safe Least Recently
Used (LRU) cache where each entry expires after a configurable TTL
(Time-To-Live).  It is built on top of Python's built-in ``collections``
and the ``threading`` lock primitives so that it can be safely used from
multiple concurrent threads.

The implementation exposes three distinct layers:

* ``LRUCache`` – the core data structure (not thread-safe by default).
* ``ThreadSafeLRUCache`` – a wrapper that adds a re-entrant ``threading.Lock``
  around every public method.
* ``pytest`` suite – a full test suite covering basic operations,
  LRU eviction policy, TTL expiry, thread safety, and edge cases.

Design Highlights
-----------------
* **LRU Policy**: Maintained with an ``OrderedDict`` where the most
  recently accessed item is moved to the end of the order.
* **TTL Expiry**: Each key carries a ``expires_at`` timestamp.  A
  background ``threading.Timer`` (or manual ``flush_expired`` call) can be
  used to clean up stale entries.  The public API supports a
  ``flush_expired`` method that performs a full sweep.
* **Thread Safety**: The wrapper acquires a single lock for the
  entire duration of each operation, guaranteeing that reads and writes
  are atomic and that no two threads can modify the internal state
  simultaneously.
* **Concurrency**: The cache itself is immutable *with respect to the
  public contract* – once an entry is added or retrieved it cannot be
  modified in place.  This simplifies the locking strategy and avoids
  the need for fine-grained reentrant locks inside the core class.
"""

        created_at: When the entry was first inserted.

    value: Any

    created_at: datetime

        self
